To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
macrophages have long been recognized as mediators of innate immune responses and that they are also involved in normal kidney organogenesis.

(1) macrophages are essential in normal kidney development and in repair after kidney injury; (2) macrophages have a dual function: they can induce inflammation and tissue damage or they can promote tissue repair and resolution of inflammation; and (3) macrophages can be polarized to a classical or alternatively activated state, with different phenotypes and functions.
Macrophages play a key role in kidney development, repair, and cancer.
